units.translation: May I perish, thirsting like dust, without breath, far from wings.
May you perish, far from gifts – may I perish. Thirsting dust.
and from my eyes thirsty drops fall
Thus I corrected for διωγμοῖσι δ᾽ ἀσφαλέας [with safe pursuits].
may she become a deliverer after seeing the pursuits
The middle future form διώσομαι [I will drive away].
Thus rightly Dobraeus for δηώσει [will ravage], which is read in the books of Strabo 4 p. 183.
he will easily drive away the Ligurian army
to pursue (in court), to accuse, to prosecute
ὄρνυται ἐπὶ πόλιν διώκων [he rushes upon the city pursuing], where by metrical indication I deleted the old gloss διώκων [pursuing]. ]
Thus Hermannus corrected for έλλαδίῳ [in Greece] (ἐλαδίω [olive] one book) κεκμῆτί [to the weary one].
he brings us some new report, pursuing with haste the guiding axles of his feet
from there I came pursuing with untiring foot
the child pursues the winged bird
Aeschylus: “Alas! Pursue with tireless foot, growing numb.”
to be pursued (pursues Robortellus) from the city, his body outraged by the bronze-forged scale
for the pursuer speaks first from the beginning
he rushes upon the city pursuing
for δμωαὶ γυναῖκες [female slaves, women] the sense demands ποῖαι γυναῖκες [what women], which Hermannus restored.
female slaves, why do you delay?
female slaves, women, good stewards of the house
so that I may not become a slave to the race of Aegyptus
and the young slave women, new to suffering
dear slave women of the house
and to see the bright light of freedom with friendly eyes from the dark veil
she speaks of some dark mist throughout the house
you have hidden the city of Susa and Ecbatana in dark grief
sunless, hateful to mortals, darknesses cover the houses
I seem to myself, or it seems to me, I think
I seem in the same sense, referred to a person

where the books of Plutarch have σύ με (or μοι) καταίθειν δοκεῖς [you seem to me to be burning me], except one which has σύ με καταίθειν μοὶ δοκεῖς [you seem to me to be burning me]. Rightly, as it seems, Grotius σύ με καιταφθιεῖν δοκεῖς [you seem to me to be about to destroy me], except that he should have written καταφθίσειν [to be about to destroy].
